sources.entry: Wave - Open-source terminal with built-in file previews, web browsing, and AI tools. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/wavetermdev/waveterm) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Wave is an open-source, AI-integrated terminal for macOS, Linux, and Windows that adds drag-and-drop workspace blocks, durable SSH sessions, file previews, a remote file editor, and an AI assistant.
summary.what_it_does: Wave is a terminal application that lets you arrange terminal blocks, editors, web browsers, and AI chat widgets in a drag-and-drop layout. It provides Wave AI, a context-aware assistant that can read terminal output and scrollback, read/write/edit files with backups and user approval, and be invoked from the CLI via `wsh ai`. Users can bring their own API keys for OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, or Azure, or run local models through Ollama and LM Studio. SSH sessions are described as durable, surviving network interruptions and Wave restarts with automatic reconnection. It includes a built-in graphical editor for remote files and an inline preview system for markdown, images, video, PDFs, CSVs, and directories. The `wsh` command system manages the workspace from the CLI and includes `wsh file` for copying and syncing files between local and remote SSH hosts. Secrets such as API keys are stored using native system backends.
use_cases: editing remote files in a GUI editor
previewing files inline in a terminal
running local LLMs with a terminal assistant
copying files between local and remote hosts
how_to_run: See the README's platform-specific installation instructions
To build from source, see the 'Building Wave Terminal' guide linked in the README
notable: Durable SSH sessions that survive network changes and restarts
Wave AI works with BYOK keys or local models and needs no account
Inline file previews and a built-in remote file editor
wsh CLI for workspace control and file sync over SSH
Native system secret storage for API keys and credentials
caveats: Minimum OS versions apply: macOS 11+, Windows 10 1809+, glibc-2.28+ Linux
Wave AI command execution is listed as coming soon, not yet available
The README says Wave AI includes free beta credits while the experience is refined
